newsitem.title: UK: Airlines must drop cargo fuel surcharge - shippers.
newsitem.headline: Airlines must drop cargo fuel surcharge - shippers.

text.p: Airlines must remove the jet fuel surcharge if they are to retain the credibility and goodwill of their customers, the European Air Shippers Council (EASC) said in a statement.
EASC secretary general Chris Welsh said "the surcharge should be withdrawn immediately."
"Aviation fuel prices have now fallen below the July 1996 high to levels lower than existed in January 1996. There can be no continued justification for retention of a fuel surcharge," he added.

"Those airlines that continue to apply the surcharge will open themselves up to warranted criticism that they are deliberately over recovering fuel costs and exploiting shippers. There is wide recognition in the air cargo industry that the fuel surcharge issue has been badly handled. Airlines now have a golden opportunity to rectify the situation and to regain the lost confidence of their customers."
"To do so air cargo carriers must remove the surcharge without delay," he stated.

The EASC heavily criticised the airline industry late last year for imposing surcharges without prior notification and the EASC said this and "widespread evidence of collusion" caused the council to lodge a formal complaint with the European Commission.

The Brussels based EASC said this complaint is being investigated by the Commission and if upheld could result in fines being imposed on airlines. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
